title: Forecasting malaria incidence in Rwanda with Neural Controlled Differential Equations and optimal control
venue: XXXI National Conference on Applications of Mathematics in Biology and Medicine – International Edition, Kościelisko, Poland
abstract: Presents a continuous-time forecasting framework for district-level malaria incidence that handles irregularly sampled survey and surveillance data, coupled to an optimal-control layer for planning ITN, IRS and treatment interventions.

title: Malaria, Economic Activity, and Public Intervention in Rwanda: A Dynamic Game Approach
abstract: Models the interaction between malaria transmission, household economic activity and government intervention in Rwanda as a dynamic game, deriving equilibrium intervention strategies and their effect on incidence and economic output.

title: A calibrated SEIRS–SEI transmission model of malaria in Rwanda with optimal intervention scheduling
authors: M. J. Muhindo, A. Nowakowski, D. Machowska
abstract: Calibrates a human–mosquito compartmental model to 30-district data (national fit error 4.2 %) and derives optimal ITN, IRS and treatment schedules by direct transcription.

title: A reproducible district-level malaria dataset for Rwanda, 2000–2022
abstract: Describes the pipeline combining Malaria Atlas Project surfaces, DHS/MIS surveys and public climate data into a 30-district, 23-year panel.
